faq.q: How often should I replace my gutters?
faq.a: Quality aluminum gutters last 20 to 40 years with minimal maintenance. If you see rust, sagging, joint leaks, or water overflowing during rain, it's time to act. Our seamless gutters have no joints to worry about.

faq.q: What is the difference between soffit and fascia?
faq.a: The fascia is the vertical board running along the lower edge of the roof — that's where gutters attach. The soffit is the horizontal surface under the roof overhang, between the wall and the fascia. Both protect your home's structure from moisture and pests. We replace both in the same visit.

faq.q: What's the difference between seamless and standard gutters?
faq.a: Standard gutters come in 10-12 foot sections joined with seams — each seam is a potential leak point. Our seamless gutters are formed on-site in one continuous piece the full length of your home, completely eliminating seams and the leaks they cause.

faq.q: Do gutter guards actually work?
faq.a: Yes — quality micro-perforated gutter guards let water through while blocking 99% of debris. They dramatically reduce maintenance and prevent the clogs that cause overflow and water damage. We strongly recommend this option if you have trees nearby.

faq.q: How long does installation take?
faq.a: For a standard single-family home, the complete installation typically takes one day. We form the gutters on-site, install the entire system, and do a full cleanup before leaving.

faq.q: What warranty is included?
faq.a: 10 years on both labor and materials. This warranty is written into our contract. If any issue arises within 10 years of installation, we return at no additional charge.

faq.q: What colors are available?
faq.a: We offer 20+ standard aluminum colors including white, beige, brown, charcoal grey, black and various wood tones. We can also match the exact color of your existing trim.

faq.q: How long does vinyl siding last?
faq.a: Heavy-gauge vinyl siding properly installed lasts 25 to 40 years without requiring paint or major maintenance. The keys are material quality and installation quality — both of which we guarantee.

faq.q: Is it really worth adding insulation at the same time?
faq.a: Absolutely. When your siding is removed, it's the only time you have direct access to your home's envelope to add insulation. The marginal cost is low compared to the energy savings over 20-30 years. We estimate a 15-25% reduction in heating bills.

faq.q: Should old siding be removed or can new siding go over it?
faq.a: We strongly recommend removing the old siding to inspect the structure underneath and detect any hidden rot, mold or water damage. Installing over existing siding without inspection is a short-term saving that can cost far more long-term.

faq.q: How long does a complete installation take?
faq.a: For a standard single-family home, installation typically takes 3 to 5 days depending on surface area and complexity. We work efficiently without cutting corners — you're updated on progress every day.

faq.q: Does vinyl siding hold up in Canadian winters?
faq.a: The heavy-gauge vinyl we use is specifically designed for northern climates. It withstands temperatures from -40°C to +50°C without cracking or warping. Panel lengths allow for proper thermal expansion.

faq.q: What's the difference between vinyl and fiber cement?
faq.a: Vinyl is lightweight, cost-effective, 100% maintenance-free and comes in many colors. Fiber cement (HardiePlank) offers a superior appearance that perfectly mimics wood, is non-combustible and even more durable, but costs more and requires repainting every 10-15 years. We advise you based on your budget and goals.

faq.q: Do you work with insurance companies?
faq.a: Yes. If your siding was damaged by hail, wind or storm and is covered by your home insurance, we can assist with the claims process and work directly with your insurer.

faq.q: How do I know if my roof needs replacing?
faq.a: Several signs indicate it's time to act: curling, cracking or missing shingles; black granules in your gutters (advanced wear); water stains on ceilings or in the attic; roof is 20+ years old; persistent moss or algae. If in doubt, we offer a free, no-obligation inspection.

faq.q: Can I stay home during the work?
faq.a: Absolutely. Roofing work is done entirely outside. You can remain at home normally. There is noise, but no interior intrusion. Most of our clients go about their day while we work.

faq.q: Why replace instead of repair?
faq.a: A partial repair on a 20-year-old roof is often ineffective: if one section fails, the rest isn't far behind. Insurance companies also sometimes refuse to cover a roof that has been repeatedly patched. A full replacement is a more financially sound decision over 20-30 years.

faq.q: What are architectural shingles and why are they better?
faq.a: Architectural (laminated) shingles are twice as thick as standard 3-tab shingles. They offer a dimensional texture mimicking slate or wood shake, superior wind resistance (130 mph vs 80 mph), and a lifespan of 25-30 years vs 15-20 years. This is our standard for all replacements.

faq.q: What exactly does your 10-year warranty cover?
faq.a: Our 10-year warranty covers all installation defects: delamination, lifting, infiltrations due to poor installation, ventilation or flashing issues. If any problem linked to our work occurs within 10 years, we return and fix it at no charge. The 20-year manufacturer warranty on materials is separate and transferable.

faq.q: Do you assist with insurance claims?
faq.a: Yes. If your roof was damaged by hail, wind or storm and is covered by your home insurance, we're experienced working with insurers. We can document the damage, provide a detailed report and guide you through the claims process.

faq.q: How long does a full replacement take?
faq.a: In the vast majority of cases, a complete roof replacement on a single-family home is done in one day (7am to 5pm). For very large homes or complex geometry (multiple hips, dormers), it may take 2 days.

articles.title: 7 Signs Your Gutters Need to Be Replaced
articles.meta_title: 7 Signs Your Gutters Need Replacing | B&T Quality Construction
articles.meta_description: Rust, leaks, overflow, sagging — discover the 7 warning signs that tell you it's time to replace your gutters before the damage gets worse.
articles.excerpt: Faulty gutters can cause thousands of dollars in foundation damage without you even noticing. Here are the 7 signs to watch for.
articles.image_alt: Rusted and clogged gutters in need of replacement
articles.intro: Your gutters play a discreet but absolutely essential role: they channel thousands of litres of rainwater away from your foundation, walls and landscaping. When they fail, the consequences can be catastrophic — and often invisible until it's too late. Here are the 7 signs that tell you replacement is necessary.

sections.heading: 1. Visible rust or cracks
sections.body: Rust is the clearest sign of an end-of-life gutter. It means the protective coating or paint has degraded and the aluminum or steel is oxidizing. Even a small crack lets water fall directly against your foundation with every rain.

sections.heading: 2. Leaks at joints or connectors
sections.body: Standard gutters are assembled in sections joined by sealed seams. These seams deteriorate over time, especially under the freeze-thaw cycles typical of Quebec winters. If you see water stains on your exterior walls at gutter level, the joints are likely the culprit.

sections.heading: 3. Water overflows during rain
sections.body: Overflow can have two causes: a clog (leaves, debris) or a poorly pitched gutter that doesn't drain toward the downspout. In both cases, if the problem persists after cleaning, replacement is often the most cost-effective long-term solution.

sections.heading: 4. Sagging or detached gutters
sections.body: Gutters that hang, tilt or pull away from the fascia indicate that the mounting hooks are rusted or that the fascia itself has rotted. In this case, gutter replacement often needs to include fascia replacement as well.

sections.heading: 5. Paint damage or stains on siding near gutters
sections.body: Peeling paint or moisture stains on your siding directly below the gutters signal a chronic leak. Water seeps between the gutter and fascia, gradually degrading the wood and cladding over time.

sections.heading: 6. Mold or water in the basement
sections.body: This is often the most costly sign. When failing gutters allow water to pool against the foundation, moisture eventually seeps into the basement — causing mold, concrete crumbling and efflorescence. Timely gutter replacement can prevent foundation repairs costing $10,000 or more.

sections.heading: 7. Your gutters are over 20 years old
sections.body: Even gutters that look fine may have lost their effectiveness after 20 years. Drainage capacity can gradually decrease without visible signs. If your home was built or your roof replaced over 20 years ago without the gutters being changed, an inspection is in order.

sections.heading: What to do now?
sections.body: If you recognize one or more of these signs, the best course of action is to act before the fall rains arrive. At B&T Quality Construction, we offer a free gutter inspection and a detailed, no-obligation quote. Our seamless aluminum gutters eliminate joints — the primary source of leaks — and carry a 10-year warranty.

articles.title: Vinyl, Fiber Cement or Aluminum: Which Siding to Choose in Quebec?
articles.meta_title: Which Exterior Siding to Choose in Quebec? Vinyl vs Fiber Cement | B&T
articles.meta_description: Complete comparison of exterior siding materials for the Quebec climate: premium vinyl, fiber cement (HardiePlank) and aluminum. Pros, cons and costs.
articles.excerpt: Choosing the right exterior siding depends on climate, budget and aesthetics. Here is a complete guide to making the right choice for your home in Quebec.
articles.image_alt: Comparison of vinyl vs fiber cement siding on a Quebec home
articles.intro: Replacing your home's exterior siding is an important decision that affects not only the appearance of your property but also its protection against the elements and its resale value. In Quebec and Ontario, the extreme climate — from -40°C in winter to +35°C in summer — imposes different selection criteria than other regions. Here is our comparative analysis of the three main materials.

sections.heading: Premium vinyl: the best value for money
sections.body: Heavy-gauge vinyl siding is by far the most popular choice in Canada, and for good reasons: it perfectly withstands freeze-thaw cycles, doesn't absorb moisture, doesn't rust and never needs painting. Current technology produces textures that perfectly mimic wood or cedar. Lifespan reaches 25 to 40 years with minimal maintenance.
list: Moderate cost — best return on investment
Zero maintenance, never needs painting
30+ colors available with wood grain texture
UV-resistant, freeze-resistant and impact-resistant
Available with integrated insulation

sections.heading: Fiber cement (HardiePlank): the premium choice
sections.body: Fiber cement is the choice for homeowners who want the authentic look of painted wood without the drawbacks of real wood. It is non-combustible, termite-resistant, rot-proof and impact-resistant. Its appearance is significantly superior to vinyl — which justifies its higher price. However, it requires repainting every 10 to 15 years.
list: Superior appearance, authentic look
Non-combustible and termite-resistant
Lifespan of 30 to 50 years
Significantly increases resale value
Requires repainting every 10-15 years

sections.heading: Factory-painted aluminum: solid and discreet
sections.body: Aluminum was the standard in the 1970s-1990s. Still popular for commercial and residential properties, it offers excellent durability with a permanent factory-painted finish. Its main drawback is that it can dent and the color selection is more limited than vinyl.
list: Very weather-resistant
Permanent factory-painted finish
Ideal for exposed or coastal properties
Can dent from impacts (hail, branches)

sections.heading: Our recommendation based on your situation
sections.body: For the vast majority of Quebec single-family homes with a reasonable budget: heavy-gauge premium vinyl is the best choice. For higher-value homes ($400,000+) or premium renovations: HardiePlank fiber cement delivers an unmatched aesthetic result. For commercial properties or extreme exposures: aluminum remains a safe bet.

sections.heading: Insulation: take advantage during installation
sections.body: Whatever material you choose, siding replacement is the ideal time to add a layer of rigid insulation beneath the new cladding. This step, easy to perform when walls are exposed, can reduce your heating bill by 15 to 25% over the next 30 years. The marginal cost is minimal compared to the energy savings.

articles.title: How to Know if Your Roof Needs Replacing: The Complete Guide
articles.meta_title: When to Replace Your Roof? Complete Guide | B&T Quality Construction
articles.meta_description: Curling shingles, granules in gutters, moisture stains — learn to recognize the signs of a roof that needs replacing and avoid costly damage.
articles.excerpt: An end-of-life roof costs more than replacement: water infiltration, mold, structural damage. Here's how to inspect yours and know when to act.
articles.image_alt: Roof inspection showing damaged and worn shingles
articles.intro: Your roof is your home's most critical protection against the elements. Unlike gutters or siding, roofing problems often develop invisibly — until the day water appears on your ceiling. By that point, interior damage can already run into thousands of dollars. Knowing how to read the warning signs lets you act before the situation spirals out of control.

sections.heading: Your roof's age: the first criterion
sections.body: A standard 3-tab shingle lasts 15 to 20 years. An architectural (laminated) shingle lasts 25 to 30 years. If your roof is approaching or exceeding these thresholds, a professional inspection is warranted even without visible signs. Deterioration can be advanced without being visible from the ground.

sections.heading: Visible signs from the ground
sections.body: Before calling a professional, here is what you can observe from your yard:
list: Curling, buckling or lifting shingles at corners
Missing or displaced shingles after a storm
Grey, dull surface — a sign of granule wear
Dark stains from algae or moss growth
Visible deflection — the roof no longer appears perfectly flat

sections.heading: Granules in gutters: a red flag
sections.body: Asphalt shingles are coated with mineral granules that protect them from UV rays and weather. Over time, these granules detach and accumulate in your gutters. If you find a large quantity of dark granules in your gutters or on the ground after rain, it means your shingles have lost their protective layer and are nearing end of life.

sections.heading: Interior signs: attic and ceilings
sections.body: Inspect your attic on a sunny day: if you can see light filtering between the roof boards, water can do the same. Also check for moisture stains on the boards or insulation batts. Inside the house, brownish ceiling stains — even faint ones — indicate an active infiltration.

sections.heading: After a storm: systematic inspection
sections.body: After every significant storm (high winds, hail, heavy snow accumulation), inspect your roof from the ground. Hail leaves characteristic circular impacts on shingles, visible through binoculars. Displaced or broken shingles after strong winds must be replaced quickly to prevent infiltration.

sections.heading: Repair or replace: when to choose what?
sections.body: Spot repair is justified when your roof is under 15 years old, the damage is localized (a few shingles) and the rest of the roof is in good condition. Beyond 20 years, or if more than 20% of the surface is affected, full replacement is generally more cost-effective and avoids repeated call-backs.

sections.heading: Free inspection by B&T Quality Construction
sections.body: If you have any doubt about the condition of your roof, contact us for a free, no-obligation inspection. Our experts assess the condition of your roof, structure and ventilation, and provide an honest report — even if the conclusion is that no replacement is needed at this time.

articles.title: Preparing Your Home's Exterior for a Quebec Winter: The Complete Checklist
articles.meta_title: Preparing Your Home's Exterior for Winter in Quebec | B&T Quality Construction
articles.meta_description: Complete checklist to protect your home before winter: gutter, roof and siding inspection. Avoid costly surprises in January.
articles.excerpt: Quebec winters are particularly demanding on your home. Here is the complete checklist to go through in October to protect your gutters, roof and siding.
articles.image_alt: Quebec home in winter with ice on gutters
articles.intro: Quebec winters are among the most brutal in the world for buildings: freezing, thawing, snow accumulation, ice storms and violent winds test every exterior component of your home. An inspection and a few interventions in September-October can prevent costly damage that typically shows up in the dead of winter, when repairs are difficult and timelines are long.

sections.heading: Gutters: priority number one before winter
sections.body: Gutters clogged with autumn leaves cause two major winter problems: ice dams and overflow damage during thaws. An ice dam forms when snowmelt water can't drain and freezes at the roof's edge, forcing water under the shingles. The consequences can be devastating.
list: Clean gutters after the last leaves have fallen (November)
Verify downspouts are clear and water flows away from the foundation
Inspect joints and fasteners — freezing worsens existing weaknesses
Consider installing gutter guards to permanently eliminate the problem

sections.heading: Roof: inspection before the first snowfall
sections.body: A weakened roof bears the weight of snow poorly. Poorly secured shingles, lifted sections or damaged membranes become infiltration points at the first thaw. Inspect from the ground with binoculars or have a professional inspect before November.
list: Replace missing or damaged shingles in the fall
Check flashings around chimneys and vents
Ensure attic ventilation is functional — it prevents ice dams
Professional inspection recommended if roof is 15+ years old

sections.heading: Exterior siding: cracks to repair before the freeze
sections.body: Water that seeps into a siding crack and freezes in winter exponentially worsens the crack. Inspect your siding in October and immediately caulk any cracks or lifting sections.
list: Inspect caulking around windows, doors and electrical outlets
Look for lifted, cracked or damaged siding panels
Check the condition of corners and trim
Caulk with a product rated for below-zero temperatures

sections.heading: Foundation and drainage: preventing spring water infiltration
sections.body: Spring snowmelt infiltrating the foundation is often caused by poor winter drainage. Make sure downspouts are extended at least 1.5 meters away from the foundation and that the ground slopes away from the house.

sections.heading: Act now to avoid emergencies in January
sections.body: Roof, gutter and siding problems identified in October can be resolved quickly and at reasonable cost. In January at -20°C, emergency interventions are more difficult, take longer and cost far more — if they're possible at all. Contact B&T Quality Construction for a free inspection before winter sets in.
